#40727 gives rise to a new interesting error in differential geometry, cannot find synthesization order for instance. I'm puzzled and don't quite know how to investigate this further. Does any of the typeclass debugging experts have a hint as to how to investigate?

Here's a version that fits into the playground... Actually, Zulip manges the formatting when pasting, and the playground link is too long for the message. So, find it attached. kindaminimal.lean
Naive attempts at minimizing (such as, extracting the goal state before the last line causing the error, or the refine StructureGroupoid.restr_mem_of_eqOn call), make the error go away.

The instance looks like the following:

variable {𝕜 : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) {n : ℕ∞} [IsManifold I n M]
variable {HG : Type*} [TopologicalSpace HG] [TopologicalSpace G] [ChartedSpace HG G]
  {EG : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup EG] [NormedSpace 𝕜 EG] (IG : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 EG HG)
  [ContMDiffSMul IG I n G M]

instance foo : IsManifold I n (orbitRel.Quotient G M) := ...

You see that you are using an assumption talking about EG and HG and IG, but these do not feature on the instance to be proved, so there is not way Lean can guess them.
(And by the way I don't understand the mathematics: the quotient of M under the G action should have strictly smaller dimension, so how could it be a manifold over I, just like M?)

(Unless G is discrete, in which case you shouldn't need any manifold structure over G to state the instance and then everything would be fine -- the correct assumption then wouldn't be ContMDiffSMul but ContMDiffConstSMul, i.e., each action of a G element should be a smooth map of M)

Sébastien Gouëzel said:

(Unless G is discrete, in which case you shouldn't need any manifold structure over G to state the instance and then everything would be fine -- the correct assumption then wouldn't be ContMDiffSMul but ContMDiffConstSMul, i.e., each action of a G element should be a smooth map of M)

In practice, I suspect this is what will be used. I agree with you, except for the question "should we have ContMDiffConstSMul"? This was discussed, and I've seen no mathematical reason to have it (I'm not aware of meaningful examples which are ContMDiffConstSMul but not ContMDiffSMul).
Well, isn't that an example? I.e., when you don't have a smooth structure on G because it's a discrete group.
But we do have a smooth structure, it's a 0-dimensional manifold. docs#ChartedSpace.of_discreteTopology is the charted space instance (for example).

Except that the model is not canonical, so in your instance you don't get access to the charted space structure. If you prefer, let me phrase it this way: to get the manifold instance on M mod G, the proper setting is ContMDiffConstSMul.
I've become convinced: #mathlib4 > Typeclasses for smooth actions: `Cont(M)Diff(Const)SMul`

I also just remembered the other application of this typeclass that I had in mind - when you have a group G acting fibrewise on a bundle E over B, registering as an instance that the smooth functions from B to G act on the smooth sections of the bundle works fine because the type of smooth functions mentions the model of G, but stating G itself acts on the smooth sections does not
That's why in #40653 I registered the former instance in full generality but the latter only in the specific case where G is the ground field with its canonical model with corners
